    e.symm.toAlgHom.comp (Subalgebra.inclusion hArange)

  ext a
  change ι (e.symm ⟨a.1, hArange a.2⟩) = a.1
  exact congrArg Subtype.val (e.apply_symm_apply ⟨a.1, hArange a.2⟩)

variable {R : Type u} {A : Type v} {B : Type w}
variable [CommSemiring R] [Semiring A] [Algebra R A] [Semiring B] [Algebra R B]

/-- A subalgebra `S` is finitely generated if there exists `t : Finset A` such that
`Algebra.adjoin R t = S`. -/
def FG (S : Subalgebra R A) : Prop :=
  ∃ t : Finset A, Algebra.adjoin R ↑t = S

theorem fg_adjoin_finset (s : Finset A) : (Algebra.adjoin R (↑s : Set A)).FG :=
  ⟨s, rfl⟩

theorem fg_def {S : Subalgebra R A} : S.FG ↔ ∃ t : Set A, Set.Finite t ∧ Algebra.adjoin R t = S :=
  Iff.symm Set.exists_finite_iff_finset

theorem fg_bot : (⊥ : Subalgebra R A).FG :=
  ⟨∅, Finset.coe_empty ▸ Algebra.adjoin_empty R A⟩

theorem fg_of_fg_toSubmodule {S : Subalgebra R A} : S.toSubmodule.FG → S.FG :=
  fun ⟨t, ht⟩ ↦ ⟨t, le_antisymm
    (Algebra.adjoin_le fun x hx ↦ show x ∈ Subalgebra.toSubmodule S from ht ▸ subset_span hx) <|
    show Subalgebra.toSubmodule S ≤ Subalgebra.toSubmodule (Algebra.adjoin R ↑t) from fun x hx ↦
      span_le.mpr (fun _ hx ↦ Algebra.subset_adjoin hx)
        (show x ∈ span R ↑t by
          rw [ht]
          exact hx)⟩

theorem fg_of_noetherian [IsNoetherian R A] (S : Subalgebra R A) : S.FG :=
  fg_of_fg_toSubmodule (IsNoetherian.noetherian (Subalgebra.toSubmodule S))

theorem fg_of_submodule_fg (h : (⊤ : Submodule R A).FG) : (⊤ : Subalgebra R A).FG :=
  let ⟨s, hs⟩ := h
  ⟨s, toSubmodule.injective <| by
    rw [Algebra.top_toSubmodule, eq_top_iff, ← hs, span_le]
    exact Algebra.subset_adjoin⟩

theorem FG.prod {S : Subalgebra R A} {T : Subalgebra R B} (hS : S.FG) (hT : T.FG) :
    (S.prod T).FG := by
  obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := fg_def.1 hS
  obtain ⟨t, ht⟩ := fg_def.1 hT
  rw [← hs.2, ← ht.2]
  exact fg_def.2 ⟨LinearMap.inl R A B '' (s ∪ {1}) ∪ LinearMap.inr R A B '' (t ∪ {1}),
    Set.Finite.union (Set.Finite.image _ (Set.Finite.union hs.1 (Set.finite_singleton _)))
      (Set.Finite.image _ (Set.Finite.union ht.1 (Set.finite_singleton _))),
    Algebra.adjoin_inl_union_inr_eq_prod R s t⟩

section

theorem FG.map {S : Subalgebra R A} (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (hs : S.FG) : (S.map f).FG := by
  let ⟨s, hs⟩ := hs
  classical
  exact ⟨s.image f, by rw [Finset.coe_image, Algebra.adjoin_image, hs]⟩

end

theorem fg_of_fg_map (S : Subalgebra R A) (f : A →ₐ[R] B) (hf : Function.Injective f)
    (hs : (S.map f).FG) : S.FG :=
  let ⟨s, hs⟩ := hs
  ⟨s.preimage f fun _ _ _ _ h ↦ hf h,
    map_injective hf <| by
      rw [← Algebra.adjoin_image, Finset.coe_preimage, Set.image_preimage_eq_of_subset, hs]
      rw [← AlgHom.coe_range, ← Algebra.adjoin_le_iff, hs, ← Algebra.map_top]
      exact map_mono le_top⟩

theorem fg_top (S : Subalgebra R A) : (⊤ : Subalgebra R S).FG ↔ S.FG :=
  ⟨fun h ↦ by
    rw [← S.range_val, ← Algebra.map_top]
    exact FG.map _ h, fun h ↦
    fg_of_fg_map _ S.val Subtype.val_injective <| by
      rw [Algebra.map_top, range_val]
      exact h⟩

theorem induction_on_adjoin [IsNoetherian R A] (P : Subalgebra R A → Prop) (base : P ⊥)
    (ih : ∀ (S : Subalgebra R A) (x : A), P S → P (Algebra.adjoin R (insert x S)))
    (S : Subalgebra R A) : P S := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := S.fg_of_noetherian
  refine Finset.induction_on t ?_ ?_
  · simpa using base
  intro x t _ h
  rw [Finset.coe_insert]
  simpa only [Algebra.adjoin_insert_adjoin] using ih _ x h

theorem FG.sup {S S' : Subalgebra R A} (hS : Subalgebra.FG S) (hS' : Subalgebra.FG S') :
    Subalgebra.FG (S ⊔ S') :=
  let ⟨s, hs⟩ := Subalgebra.fg_def.1 hS
  let ⟨s', hs'⟩ := Subalgebra.fg_def.1 hS'
  fg_def.mpr ⟨s ∪ s', Set.Finite.union hs.1 hs'.1,
    (by rw [Algebra.adjoin_union, hs.2, hs'.2])⟩

end Subalgebra

+    {F K B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
+    [CommRing B] [Algebra F B] (L : FinSubext F K) :
+    Function.Injective

+        L.1 ⊗[F] B →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] B).toLinearMap =
+        LinearMap.rTensor B L.1.val.toLinearMap := by
+    ext x b
+    rfl

+    Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap

+  exact hinj

+The factorization is an algebra map, so it can be used directly to base-change a cocycle datum. -/

+    {F K B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
+    [CommRing B] [Algebra F B]
+    (A₀ : Subalgebra F (K ⊗[F] B)) (hA₀ : A₀.FG) :
+    ∃ (M : FinSubext F K) (f : A₀ →ₐ[F] M.1 ⊗[F] B),
+      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)).comp f = A₀.val := by
+  classical
+  obtain ⟨s, hsfinite, hs⟩ := Subalgebra.fg_def.mp hA₀
+  letI : Finite s := hsfinite.to_subtype
+  obtain ⟨M, xM, hxM⟩ :=
+    exists_finSubext_tensorProduct_preimage_finite
+      (x := fun a : s => (a.1 : K ⊗[F] B))

+    Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)
+  have hmap : ι.toLinearMap = LinearMap.rTensor B M.1.val.toLinearMap := by
+    ext x b
+    rfl
+  have hsrange : s ⊆ (ι.range : Set (K ⊗[F] B)) := by

+  exact congrArg Subtype.val (e.apply_symm_apply ⟨a.1, hArange a.2⟩)

      "body": "**FGA picSharp rewire LANDED (run 0008): route-(b) conventions + two standing caveats.**\n\nState after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements \u2014 Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):\n\n- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C \u22d9 forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`. The other three are typed-sorry carriers: `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman \u00a74 `th:main`(1), true under the rational point) and the pre-existing Quot-blocked `HasDivFunctor` / `HasAbelMap`.\n- `instPicSharpRepresentable` proved by `choose_spec`; `groupSchemeStructure : CommGrpObj (PicScheme C)` proved via `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` + a `Multiplicative.ofAdd` NatIso (`picSharpCommGrpForgetIso`, naturality is `rfl` \u2014 no defeq walls anywhere in this file).\n- Consumers: quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` (synthesized from `[HasRationalPoint C]`) \u2014 `degree`/`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` in `IdentityComponent.lean` now carry it. `Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` is now a real def (axiom-clean), gated on `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`.\n\n**Caveat 1 \u2014 pointless curves:** `JacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) requires the abelian variety $J$ to exist UNconditionally, but route (b) only builds `PicScheme` for pointed $C$. For a genus-$\\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/\u00e9tale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now \u2014 record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.\n\n**Caveat 2 \u2014 `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free \u2124/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, \u00e9tale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space). The former GLOBAL `instHasSmoothProperQuotient \u27e8sorry\u27e9` (every presheaf representable!) was deleted this run (Ground-confirmed gone); the class is a use-site hypothesis only.       "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

   exact ⟨L, xA0, hxA0⟩
 
+/-- The canonical map from a finite tensor stage into the tensor product over `K` is injective.
+This is flatness of `B` over the field `F`, expressed through the tensor-product algebra map. -/
+theorem tensorProduct_map_finSubext_injective
+    {F K B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
+    [CommRing B] [Algebra F B] (L : FinSubext F K) :
+    Function.Injective
+      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B) :
+        L.1 ⊗[F] B →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] B) := by
+  have hmap :
+      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map L.1.val (AlgHom.id F B) :
+        L.1 ⊗[F] B →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] B).toLinearMap =
+        LinearMap.rTensor B L.1.val.toLinearMap := by
+    ext x b
+    rfl
+  have hinj : Function.Injective (LinearMap.rTensor B L.1.val.toLinearMap) :=
+    Module.Flat.rTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap
+      L.1.val.toLinearMap Subtype.val_injective
+  rw [← hmap] at hinj
+  exact hinj
+
+/-- A finitely generated subalgebra of `K ⊗[F] B` factors through one finite tensor stage.
+The factorization is an algebra map, so it can be used directly to base-change a cocycle datum. -/
+theorem exists_finSubext_fg_subalgebra_tensorProduct_factor
+    {F K B : Type u} [Field F] [Field K] [Algebra F K] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic F K]
+    [CommRing B] [Algebra F B]
+    (A₀ : Subalgebra F (K ⊗[F] B)) (hA₀ : A₀.FG) :
+    ∃ (M : FinSubext F K) (f : A₀ →ₐ[F] M.1 ⊗[F] B),
+      (Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)).comp f = A₀.val := by
+  classical
+  obtain ⟨s, hsfinite, hs⟩ := Subalgebra.fg_def.mp hA₀
+  letI : Finite s := hsfinite.to_subtype
+  obtain ⟨M, xM, hxM⟩ :=
+    exists_finSubext_tensorProduct_preimage_finite
+      (x := fun a : s => (a.1 : K ⊗[F] B))
+  let ι : M.1 ⊗[F] B →ₐ[F] K ⊗[F] B :=
+    Algebra.TensorProduct.map M.1.val (AlgHom.id F B)
+  have hmap : ι.toLinearMap = LinearMap.rTensor B M.1.val.toLinearMap := by
+    ext x b
+    rfl
+  have hsrange : s ⊆ (ι.range : Set (K ⊗[F] B)) := by
+    intro x hx
+    refine ⟨xM ⟨x, hx⟩, ?_⟩
+    change ι.toLinearMap (xM ⟨x, hx⟩) = x
+    rw [hmap]
+    exact hxM ⟨x, hx⟩
+  have hArange : A₀ ≤ ι.range := by
+    rw [← hs]
+    exact Algebra.adjoin_le hsrange
+  have hι : Function.Injective ι := tensorProduct_map_finSubext_injective M
+  let e : M.1 ⊗[F] B ≃ₐ[F] ι.range := AlgEquiv.ofInjective ι hι
+  let f : A₀ →ₐ[F] M.1 ⊗[F] B :=
+    e.symm.toAlgHom.comp (Subalgebra.inclusion hArange)
+  refine ⟨M, f, ?_⟩
+  ext a
+  change ι (e.symm ⟨a.1, hArange a.2⟩) = a.1
+  exact congrArg Subtype.val (e.apply_symm_apply ⟨a.1, hArange a.2⟩)
+
 /-- A finite family of tensor equalities that holds over `K` already holds over one common
 finite subextension containing the original stage. -/
